title: Bucanus: apply Christ by mind’s judgment and heart’s desire — with Wendelin and Chamier
source_text: LXXVI. Similiter Bucanus docet Christum nobis applicari, non tantum per judicium & approbationem mentis, sed etiam per cordis desiderium & apprehensionem: ut patet ex illa ejus fidei descriptione quam supra attulimus. Dum scilicet, dicit, Fidem esse ex mentis notitia & approbatione, judicioque speciali, voluntatis sive cordis desiderium & apprehensionem, qua Christum crucifixum cum beneficiis suis in Verbo & Sacramentis oblatum singuli privatim nobis ipsis applicamus. Et idem etiam hac in parte, cum Baronio & Bucano, sentire necesse est, omnes illos qui amorem & desiderium numerant inter actus fidei justificantis; quod faciunt Wendelinus, Chamierus & alii.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise Bucanus teaches that Christ is applied to us not only through the judgment and approval of the mind, but also through the desire and apprehension of the heart: as is plain from that description of faith of his which we brought forward above. When namely he says that Faith is, from the mind's knowledge and approval and special judgment, the desire and apprehension of the will or heart, by which we each privately apply to ourselves Christ crucified with his benefits offered in the Word and Sacraments. And it is necessary that all those also who number love and desire among the acts of justifying faith feel the same in this part with Baron and Bucanus; which Wendelin, Chamier, and others do.
pass_b_english: Bucanus: Christ is applied not by mind’s judgment alone but also by the heart’s desire and apprehension.
Faith = from mind’s knowledge, approval, and special judgment, the will’s desire and grasp by which each privately applies crucified Christ with his benefits offered in Word and Sacraments.
Same line as Baron for all who count love and desire among justifying faith’s acts — Wendelin, Chamier, and others.
